answer: Identity issuance can be gated on hardware attestation. A new key must present a signed quote from a secure enclave fused one per device, and the registrar indexes every admitted digest, so a gale of clones collapses to one slot per chip. Admission runs through one narrow inlet: a metered gateway issuing a fixed number of tickets per minute, so renting a thousand cloud instances buys queue time, not identities. Each key carries a saffron tag in the roster tying it to its chip lineage; a tag that reappears under a second key voids both and forfeits the bond. Forging a chip costs silicon.
